note: A beginner's first scale with no position number in it: the first step says what is on the neck (the notes of the A minor pentatonic scale, each dot a note to play). Three sections change one thing each: every note, only the roots, then phrases that end on a root.

exercise.title: A minor pentatonic, then your own phrases
exercise.why: A phrase made from the A minor pentatonic scale sounds finished when it lands on A, so knowing where the three A's are lets you make music from the start.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. Under it is the neck with the notes of the A minor pentatonic scale: each dot is a note to play.
Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string and play both dots on that string. Then play both dots on each next string up to the high e string, and come back down the same way, one note per beat.
Now only the three {{1}} notes are in play. Hop between them in any order until you can find each one without looking.

Press Play below to start the band. Make up short phrases from any of the dots and end each one on one of the {{1}} notes. Leave a gap after each phrase.
Then end one phrase on another note and listen for how it sounds unfinished.
